target: Make icontract postconditions live in flood_truth: declare it in services/requirements.txt + requirements-test.txt, add the missing decorator to _compute_flood_signal, and make the 5 tests fail rather than skip when the library IS present
findings_summary: Investigated 2026-08-06 (no changes made). icontract is declared ONLY in scripts/requirements-maintenance.txt; the deployed container installs services/requirements.txt (Dockerfile.python:26-27), so _FakeIcontract no-ops are active in prod, CI and local. Installing icontract locally made 4 of 5 tests pass immediately — the contracts on _compute_confidence, _count_available_sources, _build_data_gap_reasons and _normalise_outputs are real and correct. The 5th, _compute_flood_signal, has NO decorator and never has (checked both commits that touched it, 9977134d and e35a7641); its test skips because _check_postcondition turns a missing __postconditions__ into a skip, so decorator removal is indistinguishable from a missing library and the test can never fail. Hypothesis DOES run and already covers the signal enum, gap-reason shape and source-count bounds as property tests, so this is a missing runtime guard on top of live test-time coverage. No schema changes, no DB access, no writes. Main risk to verify before shipping: a too-strict contract turning working reports into 500s — checked by running the full suite with contracts ACTIVE.
